## 8. Actual emission count: a rate-independent global cap

Add a classical emitted-count register C. On the exact finite-K joint process, passive free evolution and actual lowering jumps conserve N+C. Only V changes it. Let M_k(t)=E[(N+C)_k]. The same weighted Cauchy-Schwarz as in the first-stage occupation proof gives

    d M_k/dt <=2k a sqrt(M_{k-1}M_k),
    M_k(t)<=(at)^(2k),
    E exp[s(N+C)]<=exp[(aT)^2(e^s-1)].

The jump part now cancels EXACTLY in a function of N+C because each counted lowering jump decreases N and increases C by one. H_S and number-preserving H commute with it. This proves, rather than assumes, a rate-independent bound for the ACTUAL emitted count. In particular, with lambda=(aT)^2,

    P(C>Jmax)<=exp[lambda(e-1)-Jmax].

Take Jmax=ceil(lambda(e-1)+log(100/epsilon))+1. Compare to the exact finite-K process frozen after this many actual jumps; never assume this MGF for the approximate implementation. An overflow has an unconditional CPTP fallback.

A fixed partition into at most ceil(vT)+p+1 control-free windows and at most Jmax actual jumps gives a deterministic call cap

    S<=ceil(vT)+p+Jmax+2.

Representative timestamps perturb the future exact capped channel by at most its finite generator norm O(v+KR) times the timestamp error. Choose the finite time word accordingly. For example, skip any residual window shorter than t_min=delta/[1+v+KR], paying its generator norm times t_min. This supplies a finite lower duration for arithmetic after a charged omission, rather than a physical minimum waiting time. A backward contractive hybrid charges at most S local isometry and clock errors, plus the exact count-tail error and tiny remaining-window omissions. This preserves arbitrary reference systems and prescribed-time instrument records without exposing private bath timestamps or normalizing rare outcomes.

## The emitted-count factorial inequality

Let `rho_c` be the unnormalized finite-cutoff density matrix conditional on `c` actual emitted photons, and set `X=N+c` in that sector. The free number-preserving Hamiltonian commutes with every function of `X`. A physical jump decreases `N` by one and increases `c` by one, so its entire Lindblad contribution to `E[g(X)]` cancels, including the no-jump anticommutator. No Poisson assumption about jump times is made.

For `F_k(x)=(x)_k`, the finite-difference identity is

    F_k(x+1)-F_k(x)=k F_{k-1}(x).

In an occupation basis, one normalized creation direction raises total `N` by one with coefficient at most `sqrt(N+1)<=sqrt(X+1)`. The identity

    (X+1)_k = (X+1)(X)_{k-1}

therefore gives, by weighted Cauchy-Schwarz over occupation, system, reference and count labels,

    |sum_c tr[rho_c Q a^dagger(g) (N+c)_{k-1}]|
      <= ||Q|| ||g|| sqrt(M_k M_{k-1}),
    M_k=E[(N+C)_k].

Missing raising transitions at the top cutoff only reduce this inequality. Apply it separately to each bounded coupling term and sum. It follows that

    dM_k/dt <= 2k a sqrt(M_k M_{k-1}).

Regularize a zero moment before dividing by its square root. Starting from vacuum and zero emitted count, induction integrates to `M_k(t)<=(at)^(2k)`. Expanding `exp(sX)` into nonnegative falling-factorial terms gives the stated MGF for all `s>=0`. A finite-`K` process has bounded jump rate, hence no finite-time explosion. Alternatively, prove the moment bound for a stopped count and take a monotone limit.

System-only instruments preserve these unconditional bounds, including their outcome labels and references; the argument never conditions on a rare observed outcome. The tail comparison is made against the exact process with a classical private jump record, so freezing an event of probability `p` costs at most `2p` in complete channel norm. It does not require a square-root probability estimate for a coherent public output field.
